marketing_faq_cost_a: On a small app, close to nothing: Workers, D1 and R2 all have free tiers that cover early traffic, and the only always-on cost is your domain. Email bills per use, and is optional.
marketing_faq_cost_q: What does it cost to run?
marketing_faq_free_a: Yes. It is MIT licensed: use it for anything, commercial products included, and keep the license file. There is no account to create and nothing phones home.
marketing_faq_shipkit_a: It is ShipKit with the paid modules taken out: Stripe and Creem payments, metered credits, the admin console with roles and permissions, API keys, affiliates, notifications and the audit log. What is left runs on its own and is yours to keep. If you later need those parts, ShipKit is a one-time purchase at shipkit.sh, on the same architecture.
marketing_faq_shipkit_q: How is it different from ShipKit?
marketing_faq_stack_a: Because D1 and R2 are bindings, not services with credentials: no connection string, no pool, no S3 keys, and local dev runs the same runtime as production. The trade is that workerd forbids some Node patterns — the template already works around the ones that matter, like runtime-eval MDX.
marketing_faq_stack_q: Why Cloudflare Workers and not a Node host?
